text:
anya: Quick heads-up — running into a flaky case on macOS where streaming requests via the Node SDK don't stop the underlying TCP connection when AbortController is called. Keeps auth refreshes from completing.

sam: ugh. repro steps?

anya: minimal repro: start a streaming chat, call controller.abort() after first chunk, then the process stays open and we see a pending socket in lsof. Happens only on Darwin in our CI images.

matt: interesting, which transport are you using? undici or node-fetch polyfill?

anya: undici (v5). We pass the AbortSignal from the SDK into underlying fetch, but looks like the stream body isn't being drained / closed consistently.

lucy: i've seen similar with older node versions where `res.body.cancel()` wasn't invoked. Could be a mismatch between our stream cancellation and undici's `body.destroy()` semantics.

sam: can you paste the call site? small snippet is fine.

anya: sure — condensed: 

```js
const controller = new AbortController();
const stream = client.chat.stream({ messages }, { signal: controller.signal });
stream.on('data', (chunk) => { controller.abort(); /* abort after first chunk */ });
```

matt: so SDK stream is an EventEmitter wrapper around the fetch ReadableStream. If we abort, fetch should reject, but if the user handler doesn't `close()` our emitter we might leak.

lucy: another vector: our auth refresh task runs on a separate timer. If the socket linger blocks key rotations (KMS handshake), that could cause token refresh to queue and eventually fail.

anya: exactly — observed a backlog of refresh requests in logs.

sam: quick mitigation: ensure we call both `res.body.cancel()` and `res.body.getReader().cancel()` where available, and also `socket.destroy()` on Node net.Socket if attached. Can we add that in the SDK's stream teardown path?

matt: yes, but be careful cross-runtime. For browser we must only use the ReadableStream cancel. For Node/undici there is `body.destroy()` or `body.cancel()` depending on version. I'd add feature-detection helpers.

lucy: also check our retry layer — if abort triggers a retry, we must not restart auth refresh until teardown completed. Maybe mark the request as "aborted" so auth refresh doesn't attach.

anya: good call. I'll draft a minimal patch to the teardown routine to: 1) mark state aborted, 2) cancel body if present, 3) destroy socket if present, 4) suppress retries for aborted requests.

sam: please add a small integration test that runs on macOS runner or in a Darwin container: start stream, abort, assert process exits within Xs and no pending sockets. Add logs for each teardown step.

matt: add a short comment referencing Go/Python behavior: in Go we use context cancellation which immediately cancels the http.Request; Python aiohttp needs explicit `resp.content.release()` in some cases. Good to document differences in our SDK docs.

lucy: for rollout, can we feature-flag the stricter teardown behind an env var `RW_STRICT_TEARDOWN=1` so infra can test before full rollout?

anya: yep. I'll open PR and request reviews from @matt and @lucy. CI bot, can you run the macos-matrix for this branch please?

ci-bot: Received request to run job `macos-matrix` for branch `fix/stream-teardown-215678`. Queued.

sam: thanks. Also add a note in the SDK CHANGELOG about altering teardown semantics and the env toggle. We'll need to coordinate with devex docs.

anya: will do. Assigning self to the PR, expect draft in ~2h.

matt: once up, I'll add a small Go and Python smoke test to ensure parity in cancellation semantics.

lucy: and I'll add an observability metric for "teardown_completed" with labels {runtime, aborted:true|false} so we can watch the rollout.

anya: awesome — thanks team.

sam: quick follow-up: does this affect streaming retries? If we suppress retries for aborted requests, we should ensure client-level retries for transient network errors still work.

matt: yes — logic: if state === aborted then no retry; else existing retry policy applies.

anya: got it. PR incoming.
